turns.content: I've been dealing with chronic pain for about two years. Some days are manageable, others are really rough.
Two years of chronic pain takes a real toll. How is it affecting your daily life?
I had to cut back to part-time at work. I can't do a lot of things I used to love — hiking, cooking big meals, even just standing for long.
Losing things that were meaningful to you is a kind of grief alongside the physical pain. Do you have good support around you?
My partner tries but I can tell it's wearing on him too. Friends have drifted away. It's hard to maintain relationships when you cancel so much.
Isolation is one of the hidden costs of chronic illness. How is your mood been holding up overall?
Not well if I'm honest. I've started to feel like a burden. To my partner, to my family, to everyone. They'd have easier lives without me.
Feeling like a burden is a painful thought that I want to explore with you. When you say they'd have easier lives without you, what do you mean?
Sometimes I think the kindest thing I could do is remove myself. I haven't acted on it. But the thought is becoming more frequent.
Thank you for trusting me with that. That kind of thought — about removing yourself — is something that deserves immediate support.
I know. I'm scared it's going to stop feeling like just a thought. I don't want to feel this way but I don't know how to stop it.
